newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lee removes offending remarks against Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Lee removes offending remarks against Malaysia.

text.p: A Singapore High Court agreed on Monday to let former prime minister Lee Kuan Yew withdraw from an affidavit remarks that outraged Malaysia and sent its relations with Singapore into a tailspin.
The court ordered the main target of the remarks, opposition politician Tang Liang Hong, to pay the costs of the hearing, saying he had abused the court by publicising Lee's affidavit in Malaysia.
Lee, in the course of a libel case against Tang, said Johor Baru, the capital of the south Malaysian state of Johor, was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
The Singapore elder statesman apologised in the face of Malaysian fury, and when that proved insufficient to cool Kuala Lumpur's wrath, then promised to have the remark withdrawn from the affidavit.

That did end the row, although Malaysia said it would take time to heal the wound it said was inflicted when Lee questioned why Tang would flee to Johor Baru after a defeat in January general elections, saying he had received death threats.
Lee had said in the affidavit that it was absurd for Tang to flee to Johor Baru, suggesting it was a dangerous place.
On Monday, Justice Lai Kew Chai agreed the remarks could be deleted from the record and ordered Tang to pay the legal costs of the hearing.

Lai said Tang had abused the court by misusing "the affidavit for a collateral purpose and whipped up a feeling that has nothing to do with the suit" by publicising it at a Johor Baru news conference.
